neighbours.label: a preposition that attaches to an event or contest noun and introduces its opponent, place or topic (game against, win over, fight against, events in, the thing about), as against the same preposition attached to a verb
fire: Thousands watched Sunday's match against Liverpool on a big screen.
The coach praised the team after its victory over Denver.
Tickets for next week's game against Seattle sold out quickly.
The protests in Chile were front-page news for a week.
He was injured in the third round of his bout against the champion.
Their surprise win over the defending champions shocked everyone.
Local papers covered the festival in Galway in great detail.
Her final race against the clock decided the gold medal.
quiet: Thousands of fans pushed against the gates before the stadium opened.
The coach jumped over the bench to celebrate with his players.
Most of the council argued against the plan to close the school.
The students marched in the rain all the way to the capitol.
He leaned hard against the door until it finally opened.
The horse leapt over the fence and ran into the field.
Local farmers protested against the new water tax.
Her brother complained about the noise from the street.

predictions: fire 0.5-1.0 on 'against/over/in/about' right after a noun like game, win, match, events; the same prepositions after verbs (leaned against, voted against) below 0.1
short: preposition after an event noun (vs after a verb)
